consensus: Kianne is built as an instant-speed, draw-burst value deck, not as Voltron. EDHREC's 970 decks list four themes - Wheels 93, +1/+1 Counters 47, Cantrips 30, Card Draw 25 - and edh.wiki gives the same pool a fifth, Flash at 5%; EDHREC's Flash page is 17 decks and its Voltron page is 10, about 1% of the pool. Her highest-synergy cards are Wilderness Reclamation (64%/55%), Wavebreak Hippocamp (47%/47%), Rashmi, Eternities Crafter (47%/44%) and Body of Knowledge (45%/42%), and the first three pay off casting spells on other players' turns rather than attacking. The read the data supports is that the EVEN half of her text - noncreature flash - is the ability people build around, the draw trigger is a rider, and the counters get spread across draw-triggered bodies rather than stacked on her. The wheels plurality is the burst version of the same idea: Windfall flashed in at an opponent's end step is seven draw triggers at once. Those decks win with Simic Ascendancy (45% of the wheels bucket), Psychosis Crawler (37%) or an Overwhelming Stampede alpha strike (40%) - not with commander damage.

findings.claim: The Voltron theme is a rounding error in her pool: EDHREC's Voltron page is 10 decks against 970 analysed, and the four themes EDHREC lists for her (Wheels 93, +1/+1 Counters 47, Cantrips 30, Card Draw 25) contain no Voltron entry. The build the pilot has is not what the world builds.

Her top synergy cards are instant-speed payoffs, which says the ability builders value is the EVEN half - noncreature flash - not the odd half and not the counters. Wavebreak Hippocamp draws on your first spell during EACH opponent's turn; Geyser Drake makes spells cost 1 less on turns other than yours; Rashmi triggers on the first spell each turn, which flash lets you have on all four turns of a rotation. None of the three cares how big Kianne is.

The wheels theme is 93 decks - the largest EDHREC lists for her - and its own page shows a draw-burst engine, not a Voltron shell. Its high-synergy cards are Brainstorm 83%/68%, Windfall 68%/64%, Wavebreak Hippocamp 65%/64%, Body of Knowledge 65%/62% and Enter the Enigma 56%/54%; its top cards add Arcane Denial 65%/42% and Growth Spiral 77%/33%. The mechanic is that a wheel is many draw triggers on one card, and every draw-triggered permanent fires alongside Kianne - which is why Body of Knowledge (P/T equal to hand size, no maximum hand size) and Chasm Skulker sit this high. Kianne's noncreature flash also lets a sorcery-speed wheel be cast at an opponent's end step, after they have committed their hand.

Even the 10 Voltron decks are half a card-draw deck: their own top cards are Growth Spiral 90%, Prime Speaker Zegana 70%/60% synergy (already in the 99) and Swiftfoot Boots 70%/45% (already in the 99), with Hadana's Climb 50%/47% the only Voltron-specific card above 40% synergy. The protection and evasion suite is thin and split - Shadowspear 40%, Winged Boots 40%, Whispersilk Cloak 30%, Lightning Greaves 30%, Aqueous Form 20% (already in the 99), Alpha Authority 20%. At n=10 a percentage is a count, so 40% is four decks and none of these is a consensus pick.

findings.claim: Of the sources located, the only one arguing for Voltron argues for it with hedges. Johnny Garcia's TheGamer guide (2024-10-18) states 'The primary win condition of the deck is winning through dealing 21 commander damage', then names two alternate wins in the same deck - 'Triskaidekaphile wins the game if you start your turn with 13 cards' and 'you can also win with Simic Ascendancy if it has 20 counters on it' (Simic Ascendancy is already in the 99). It names the reliance problem itself: 'The biggest downside of the deck is the heavy reliance on your commander... if it ever gets removed, you can struggle to stay in the game.' It has three sections (Decklist / Key Cards / How To Play The Deck), recommends generic Voltron equipment, and touches parity once - 'being able to cast them on odd power is a nice backup utility'. It is competent deck-guide copy, not a considered case for Voltron over the alternatives: it never compares the plan to a value build, never counts how many draws 21 damage costs, and never engages with what a counter multiplier does to her parity.

Two Simic lines on her EDHREC combo page are win conditions rather than curiosities, and neither uses a Game Changer. Fathom Mage + Wizard Class is listed as producing infinite card draw, infinite draw triggers and near-infinite +1/+1 counters (Wizard Class level 3 puts a counter on target creature on each draw; Fathom Mage draws on each counter put on it). Body of Research + Simic Ascendancy is listed as 'win the game at the beginning of your next upkeep' - Body of Research makes one token carrying counters equal to your library size, and Simic Ascendancy (already in the 99) reads counters put on creatures you control. Both route through counters put on creatures, and neither needs Kianne to connect in combat.

Alternate wins that read her draw output directly are part of the published build and cost one card each. Triskaidekaphile wins at your upkeep on exactly thirteen cards in hand and gives no maximum hand size; Twenty-Toed Toad wins on attack with twenty counters on it OR twenty cards in hand and sets your maximum hand size to twenty; Wizard Class and Body of Knowledge also remove the hand-size cap. In a deck that draws enough to make a 21-power commander, these are the same resource read a second way and they do not have to survive combat.

EDHREC's Flash theme page is 17 decks, more than the Voltron page's 10, and edh.wiki lists Flash as a fifth playstyle at 5% where it lists Wheels 28%, +1/+1 Counters 14%, Cantrips 9% and Card Draw 7%. The Flash page's high-synergy list is Wavebreak Hippocamp 71%/70%, Wilderness Reclamation 76%/67% (already in the 99), Rashmi 59%/56%, Body of Knowledge 53%/50%, Brainstorm 59%/44% and Windfall 47%/43% - the same cards as the wheels list, which is what makes 'flash value' and 'wheels' one archetype with two speeds rather than two archetypes.

How her decks actually win, per the wheels page's own numbers: Simic Ascendancy 45%/32% (counter-based alternate win), Overwhelming Stampede 40%/27% (an alpha strike across the whole board, not commander damage) and Psychosis Crawler 37%/33% (each opponent loses 1 life per card YOU draw, so a wheel is a burn spell). None of the three is a 21-commander-damage plan, and Psychosis Crawler and Overwhelming Stampede both convert the same draw output without needing Kianne to survive or connect.

known_failure_modes: Commander dependence, named by the one Voltron source: 'The biggest downside of the deck is the heavy reliance on your commander. As with all Voltron decks, it's what the rest of the deck is built around, so if it ever gets removed, you can struggle to stay in the game.' Its own remedy is to hold her until protection is up - 'it's important to wait until you're sure you can protect it (either with permanents or counterspells) before you cast it' - which delays the draw trigger the whole deck is built on.

Counters do not survive a zone change, and commander damage does not accumulate across recastings. A bounce or an exile resets Kianne to 2/2 and every draw spent growing her is gone, whereas the same draws in a wheels build are already cards in hand and life already lost to Psychosis Crawler. No source states this; it follows from the commander's own text and from the reliance quote above.

The Voltron sample has not converged on protection: Whispersilk Cloak and Lightning Greaves are 3 decks of 10 each, Shadowspear and Winged Boots 4 of 10. Even the builders who chose the plan disagree about how to keep her alive.

The wheels build's own hazard is symmetry - a wheel refills three opponents too. The wheels page's answer is Narset, Parter of Veils, which TheGamer also names (note: Narset is a Game Changer, so she moves the deck's bracket floor): 'Windfall pairs especially well with Narset, Parter of Veils, which prevents opponents from drawing more than one card each turn.' Not located: any source measuring how often that asymmetry actually lands.
contested: Whether Voltron is a real plan for her. Inclusion data says 10 decks of 970 and no Voltron entry among the five themes EDHREC and edh.wiki list; TheGamer's guide says 'If you're looking for a different take on Voltron, look no further than Kianne, Corrupted Memory' and 'the primary win condition of the deck is winning through dealing 21 commander damage'. These do not disagree about facts - the guide is a build article and never claims its build is the popular one - but they are the only two positions located, and the disagreement is 1 article against 970 decklists.

Whether the draw trigger is the point or a rider. The wheels theme (93 decks) wants many draws at once, which is Kianne-specific; the Wavebreak / Rashmi / Geyser Drake block wants flash, which is the other half of her text and does not need the trigger at all. No located source reconciles them, and the same cards appear on both theme pages.

gaps: PARITY IS UNDISCUSSED. Four EDHREC pages, edh.wiki and TheGamer's guide were read and none treats even/odd as a resource. TheGamer gives it one clause ('being able to cast them on odd power is a nice backup utility'); edh.wiki's page contains no parity discussion at all. Nobody found says whether builders avoid counter multipliers, run an even number of 'that many plus one' effects to keep the increment odd, or deliberately lock her EVEN to keep noncreature flash on. edh.wiki does list Hardened Scales among her counter cards (+9% synergy) with no comment on what it does to her parity, which is weak evidence that the interaction is simply not on builders' radar. Settling this needs a stack scenario or a targeted forum search, not more EDHREC.

The derivation the sources do not make, offered as reasoning rather than as a citation: her power is 2 (even) at base, so with a plain +1 per draw the parity ALTERNATES and both flash modes are live on alternating draws. One 'that many plus one' effect makes the increment 2, and any doubling of the increment or of the existing counters makes power 2+2c - even forever, creature flash off for good. Two such 'plus one' effects restore an odd increment (1+2=3). No source was found stating this; it is arithmetic on the printed text and should be confirmed by resolve-stack before it is relied on.
No dedicated wheels PRIMER for Kianne was located - only EDHREC's theme page. The wheels reading rests on inclusion data plus card text, not on an author arguing it.

No reddit or forum thread about her was reachable through search; two searches returned only retail and card-database pages. Deck-hosting sites (Archidekt, MTGGoldfish) surfaced in search but were not fetched, so no individual decklist is cited here.

EDHREC's combos page total could not be pinned down: the brief cites 225 combos and the page as read reported a larger figure. Only the ten combos named in the source entry were actually read, so the total is not stated in this artifact.

Bracket check on the named cards was done only for Game Changer status: of the 31 cards named in findings, exactly one - Narset, Parter of Veils - is flagged game_changer in cards.csv. Whether any of these adds moves this deck's recorded bracket must be settled with bracket-check, not here.

_checked_against.note: 'already in the 99' was checked against cards.json as it stood, which describes the V2 working draft (Simic Ascendancy, Genji Glove, Karn's Bastion, Mana Confluence, Flooded Grove in; Soul's Majesty, Aetherize, Haunted Cloak, Tamiyo's Safekeeping, Sower of Temptation out). If the deck is restored to V1 those five adds are NOT in the 99 and the parentheticals naming them as present go stale. Added by the orchestrator; no finding was altered.
